content:
Alex: FYI ran per-channel INT8 calibration on a prod-ish sample. Perf looks worse than per-tensor for the r1 kernels.

Maria: numbers?

Alex: model=redwood-7b-8k, mixed seqs (mostly 16/64, some 512/1024). per-tensor INT8 (prod) = 620 tok/s, p50 9.8ms, p95 38ms. per-channel INT8 = 540 tok/s, p50 10.6ms, p95 47ms. FP8 path is 750 tok/s.

Jordan: profile shows an extra transpose/copy in the per-channel kernels. KV cache alignment changed, so we copy into aligned buffers more often.

Sam: can you share flamegraphs? my guess: per-channel added packing work that doesn't amortize for small batch/short seq.

Alex: flamegraph link: https://ci.redwoodinfra/internal/ci/5678
perf top snip:

```
kernel_gemm_int8         40.8%
transpose_pack           19.3%
kv_cache_copy            12.1%
softmax                  9.4%
misc                     18.4%
```

Deepti: what was the calibration set? uniform sample or stratified?

Alex: uniform 5k recent examples, ended up with ~1% extreme long-tail outliers. Proposal: switch to stratified by sequence length + route intent, cap outliers, and keep small adversarial set for accuracy checks.

Sam: uniform will bias toward short chats and hide dynamics for mid/long. stratify by seq-length is sensible. Also consider per-layer weighting: layers with high dynamic range should have more samples.

Jordan: tradeoff: per-channel helps numeric quality but adds runtime complexity. Another approach: compute per-layer activation histograms offline and only enable per-channel quant for layers with dynamic-range ratio > threshold.

Maria: we should also look at batching heuristics. If we increase min-batch to 4 for short sequences, the packing overhead may be amortized. But that impacts latency.

Sam: I can run latency/throughput sims for min-batch 1..8 against our SLO model.

Ops-Bot: ran small fleet A/B with stratified calib (2k short, 2k mid, 1k long, capped outliers). Results: throughput 585 tok/s, p95 41ms. Quality evals: BLEU/ROUGE stable, slight drift on rare intent set.

Deepti: hybrid idea: default per-tensor, fall back to per-channel for flagged layers from offline histograms. That avoids global kernel path change.

Jordan: or fix the KV alignment/copying so per-channel path doesn't force extra memmoves. Padded allocations or thread-local aligned buffers could avoid transposes.

Alex: agrees. Proposed action items:
- Sam: run batch/latency sims for min-batch=1..8 (EOD)
- Jordan: prototype aligned-buffer reuse for per-channel path, microbench (48h)
- Deepti/Maria: finalize stratified sampling + outlier cap + per-layer histogram rule (72h)
- Eng-Platform/Eng-ML: add rollout gate to enable hybrid quant per-model

CI-Bot: perf test for PR #4521 (hybrid-path proto) finished: memcpy in kernel path -9%, token throughput +6% on synthetic long-seq bench.

Alex: excellent. please tag me on immediate patch experiments. don't flip prod to per-channel wholesale until kernel/mem work is validated.

Sam: posting sim outputs here when ready.

Deepti: plan is hybrid + stratified sampling + kernel/mem fixes, conservative rollout with KV-copy % and p95 telemetry.

Alex: closing this thread; will open follow-ups per action items. :thumbsup:
